high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of August 2, 2026 — Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank and Others
high.summary:
As of early August 2026, Vietnam's deposit rate market remains broadly stable with no significant new adjustments observed. A survey across 34 banks shows 12-month deposit rates ranging from a low of 3.7% p.a. to a high of 7.8% p.a. — a spread of 410 basis points reflecting significant divergence between state-owned and private/smaller banks. ACB leads the market at 7.8% p.a. for 12-month tenors, followed by Saigonbank (7.2%) and Bac A Bank (7.1%). Seven banks in total now offer 7.0% or above for 12-month deposits, including MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB. The four state-owned commercial banks — Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, and VietinBank — continue to maintain a unified rate schedule. Competitive pressure remains concentrated among small-to-mid-sized banks. **Implications:** The persistent rate differential between state and private banks signals continued liquidity competition. Elevated deposit rates at private banks could sustain upward pressure on lending rates, potentially dampening credit growth. For VND bond investors, sticky deposit rates at this level imply limited near-term room for government bond yield compression. Watch for any SBV guidance on rate caps or liquidity injections.

---

high.title: Vietnam Stock Market to Welcome Major September Event: FTSE Russell Emerging Market Upgrade — Expert Outlook
high.summary:
On August 21, 2026, FTSE Russell will officially announce the constituent stocks to be included in the FTSE Global Equity Index Series (FTSE GEIS) under the Emerging Market category, with the reclassification taking effect September 21, 2026. Vietnam's upgrade from Frontier to Emerging Market status is expected to attract approximately **USD 6 billion** in total inflows from both active and passive funds. Of this, ETFs tracking FTSE indices alone are projected to deploy roughly **USD 1.5 billion** over a one-year phased timeline. VinaCapital's Senior Investment Director Dinh Duc Minh cautioned that market impact will likely be **gradual rather than immediate**, suggesting a step-by-step capital deployment rather than a sharp one-off surge. For international fund managers, this is a critical event to monitor: the phased inflow of foreign capital has direct implications for **VND demand, FX stability, and equity valuations**. Elevated foreign buying could support VND appreciation pressure, reduce SBV intervention needs, and compress government bond yields via improved risk appetite. Watch the August 21 FTSE announcement closely as a near-term catalyst.

---

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of August 3rd: LPBank Raises Rates Across Multiple Tenors — Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank and Others
high.summary: The deposit rate market entered August with a notable upward move as LPBank raised rates across multiple tenors — the first significant adjustment after an extended period of stability. As of August 3rd, LPBank lifted its 6-month and 9-month rates from 6.8% to 7.1% p.a., its 12-month rate from 6.9% to 7.3% p.a., and its 18-month rate from 6.95% to 7.25% p.a. This positions LPBank as the second-highest deposit rate offerer in the 12-month segment, trailing only ACB, which continues to lead the market at 7.8% p.a. for 12 months, with 7.6% and 7.7% for 6- and 9-month tenors respectively. Saigonbank ranks third at 7.2%, followed by Bac A Bank at 7.1%. A cluster of banks — MBV, VCBNeo, PGBank, and VIB — all sit at the 7.0% threshold.

high.title: Overnight Interbank Rate Falls to 0.7% in Late July; SBV Shifts to Net Injection of VND 12.3 Trillion via OMO
high.summary:
The Vietnam Interbank Market Research Association (VIRA) reported that during the week of July 27–31, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) shifted its Open Market Operations (OMO) stance to net injection mode, pumping a net VND 12,322.94 billion into the banking system via the collateralized securities channel. The SBV offered VND 61,000 billion across 7-day, 42-day, 63-day, and 91-day tenors, holding the OMO rate steady at 4.5% per annum. Total bids accepted reached VND 48,341.63 billion against VND 36,018.69 billion in maturities. Notably, the SBV continued to refrain from issuing treasury bills (T-bills), reinforcing its accommodative liquidity posture. Total outstanding OMO balance now stands at VND 172,530.36 billion. The overnight interbank rate declining to 0.7% signals ample system liquidity and is consistent with a dovish near-term policy stance. **For FX traders:** ultra-low interbank rates reduce the carry incentive to hold VND, which could exert mild depreciation pressure on VND/USD if sustained. **For bond investors:** abundant liquidity supports continued demand for government bonds and may compress short-end yields further. Watch whether the SBV reintroduces T-bill issuance as a signal of any pivot toward tightening.

---

medium.title: Vietnamese Stock Market After Its Steepest Drop of the Year: Will August Offer Relief?
medium.summary: The VN-Index closed July on a positive note, rebounding 2.95% in the final week to settle at 1,735 points, recovering back above the key 1,700 level after suffering its sharpest single-period decline of 2026. The recovery was broad-based, with gains across banking, technology, steel, retail, real estate, insurance, energy, and fertilizer sectors. The primary catalyst was Q2 earnings season, with large-cap companies reporting solid profit growth that drew capital back into the market. However, liquidity remained selective — money flowed predominantly into fundamentally sound names, while stocks lacking a clear catalyst continued to underperform. Weekly trading volume fell approximately 10.3% versus the prior week, suggesting the rally lacked full conviction. For bond and FX traders, the equity rebound is worth monitoring as a sentiment indicator: sustained VN-Index strength could attract renewed foreign portfolio inflows, providing marginal support to VND. The key question entering August is whether earnings momentum can sustain the recovery or whether macro headwinds reassert pressure.

medium.title: VinaCapital Expert: History Shows Vietnamese Equities Can Rally 80–100% After Major Corrections
medium.summary: VinaCapital's Senior Investment Director, Dinh Duc Minh, speaking at the FunInsider forum organized by Fmarket, drew comparisons between the current market correction and prior major drawdowns — including the COVID-19 selloff, the Van Thinh Phat / corporate bond crisis, and last year's sharp decline triggered by U.S. tariffs on Vietnamese goods. His key finding: in each prior episode, the market was pushed into deeply discounted valuation territory, followed by recovery cycles lasting 1–2 years with cumulative gains from the trough of 80–100%. He noted that each downturn had distinct root causes — e.g., the 2018 episode was driven by trade war tensions and elevated U.S. interest rates — implying the recovery trajectory can vary. For international fund managers, this historical framing is relevant context: if Vietnamese equities are indeed in a valuation trough, patient positioning in VN-Index-linked instruments could offer asymmetric upside, though the pace of recovery is likely to be gradual rather than sharp.

medium.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of August 1, 2026 — Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, MB, Sacombank, HDBank and Others
medium.summary: This August 1 rate survey corroborates the August 2 data, confirming that the deposit rate landscape entered the new month with no material changes following localized adjustments seen in July. ACB again leads at 7.8% p.a. for 12-month deposits, with the same seven-bank cluster at or above 7.0%. State-owned banks (Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, VietinBank) maintain a coordinated rate of 6.8% p.a. for 12-month tenors, indicating implicit policy alignment. The stability across consecutive days reinforces a picture of a market in a holding pattern — neither tightening nor easing — which is relevant context for assessing VND funding costs and the bond yield curve outlook.

medium.title: Gold Prices — Smooth Ring Gold and SJC Bar Gold Today, August 2
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices remain elevated with SJC gold bars quoted at VND 137–141 million/tael (buy/sell), while smooth ring gold (9999) trades at VND 136–138 million/tael (buy) and VND 140–142 million/tael (sell). International spot gold closed the week at USD 4,041/oz, supported by dip-buying and cooling inflation data. The domestic-international price premium remains a watch point for the SBV, as persistent large premiums have historically prompted regulatory intervention in Vietnam's gold market. Elevated gold demand can also serve as a partial proxy for VND sentiment and inflation expectations — relevant context for FX and rates traders monitoring household asset allocation behavior.

medium.title: A Paradox Is Opening a Major Opportunity in the Stock Market — Where Is Money Flowing?
medium.summary: The VN-Index had a difficult July 2026, briefly touching 1,650 points before closing the month down nearly **7%** — a move the manager of the billion-dollar Pyn Elite Fund described as a "Horrible July." The paradox highlighted is that markets sold off despite broadly positive Q2 earnings: FiinGroup data (as of July 29) shows aggregate post-tax profit for 672 listed companies rose **25.6% year-on-year**, with non-financial sectors up 36.1% and financials up 10.7%. Blue-chip names including Vinhomes and Mobile World reported record or near-record profits. The disconnect between fundamentals and price action suggests **sentiment and liquidity dynamics** — rather than earnings — are driving near-term VN-Index weakness. For bond and FX traders, sustained domestic equity outflows could weigh on risk appetite and indirectly pressure VND if foreign investors are net sellers.

medium.title: Vietnamese Equities Enter a Historically Strong Month — Sector Rotation in Focus
medium.summary: ABS Securities' Investment Banking Director Nguyen The Minh notes that historical data shows the VN-Index has a **high probability of gains in August**, with an average monthly return exceeding 2%, particularly for mid- and small-cap stocks. On the macro front, the **US Federal Reserve held rates steady at 3.50–3.75%** at its July meeting — the fifth consecutive hold — though three FOMC members dissented in favor of a 25bps hike, keeping a **September Fed rate hike on the table**. This is directly relevant to Vietnam: any Fed tightening in September could strengthen the USD, renew depreciation pressure on VND, and complicate SBV's FX management heading into the FTSE rebalancing window. Traders should monitor Fed communication closely alongside domestic equity momentum.

medium.title: Acting CEO of a Major Bank Submits Resignation, Effective August 1st — Eximbank (EIB)
medium.summary: Eximbank (ticker: EIB) announced that Mr. Tran Tan Loc, its Acting CEO, submitted his resignation on July 30, 2026, citing personal reasons, effective August 1st. Mr. Loc, born in 1969 and holding a PhD in Finance and Banking, has been with Eximbank since 1994 — one of the longest-serving senior executives in the bank's history. He previously served as Standing Deputy CEO from 2007 and has acted as CEO on multiple occasions during leadership transitions. This leadership change at Eximbank introduces near-term governance uncertainty at a mid-tier listed bank, which could weigh on EIB share price sentiment. While not a systemic risk event, investors in Vietnamese equities and the broader banking sector should monitor whether this triggers a broader leadership reshuffle or regulatory scrutiny, particularly given Eximbank's historically complex shareholder and management dynamics.

medium.title: SJC Gold Bar and Ring Gold Prices on August 3rd: Domestic Gold Rises VND 500,000/Tael Across Major Retailers
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices in Vietnam rose uniformly in the afternoon session of August 3rd, with most major retailers — SJC, DOJI, Bao Tin Minh Chau, Bao Tin Manh Hai, and Phu Quy — raising prices by VND 500,000/tael on both buy and sell sides. SJC gold bars are now quoted at VND 137.5–141.5 million/tael, while SJC ring gold is at VND 137–141 million/tael. Bao Tin Minh Chau held prices flat at VND 138.3–142.3 million/tael. The rally in domestic gold prices tracks global gold market momentum and is relevant to VND dynamics, as elevated gold demand historically pressures the dong via increased USD demand for gold imports and potential gray-market FX activity. The SBV's management of the gold-FX nexus remains a key structural risk factor for VND stability.
